goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Group creation ignores params[:alias_level], so non-default alias levels sent by the client are silently replaced with the default

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the create method in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb, the code sets group.name and group.visible from params, but does not set group.alias_level. In contrast, the update method does handle alias_level: 'group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?'. This means when creating a new group, any alias_level value sent by the client is ignored and the group will use the default alias_level (0). This is a real inconsistency/bug where the create action doesn't handle a parameter that the update action does handle.

adjudication_records.issue_text: After deleting the only member on the last page, findMembers() reuses an out-of-range offset and leaves the UI on a blank page instead of returning to the last populated page

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, when removeMember is called, it calls self.findMembers() after the deletion. In findMembers(), the offset is calculated as: `var self = this, offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0));` - but this uses the OLD user_count before the server responds with updated counts. After deletion, if you were on the last page with only one member, the offset would still be set to the old value. When the server responds, it updates user_count, limit, offset from result.meta. However, the issue is that the offset sent to the server could be out of range if the user_count decreased. The server would need to handle this gracefully. Looking at the Ruby controller's members action, it just uses the offset directly without clamping to the new total. So if you delete the last member on page 2 (offset=50) and now there are only 49 users total, requesting offset=50 would return an empty result. The findMembers doesn't automatically adjust to go back to a valid page. This is a real edge case bug.
